title: Introduce tenant-fallback-sampler-and-traffic-shepherd
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Adds a probabilistic tenant fallback sampler and a traffic shepherd controller that coordinates graceful regional failovers and KV preservation. Includes telemetry events, dashboards, and a small hotfix for circuit-state flapping.
description: Motivation: during recent regional surges we observed sharp SLO regressions caused by wholesale failovers and aggressive global load-shedding; this PR introduces two cooperating pieces: (1) a tenant-fallback-sampler which selects a bounded fraction of requests per tenant for controlled fallback to lower-cost/compatible model variants and (2) a traffic-shepherd controller that sequences regional handoffs, preserves KV prefix state during partial evacuations, and ramps traffic according to SLO telemetry. The sampler is probabilistic with configurable per-tenant caps and time-decay so we can gather quality telemetry and allow staged rollouts without impacting steady clients. The shepherd implements an epoch token that prevents rapid circuit flips and coordinates graceful KV draining and resumptions across zones. This PR also contains a small hotfix to the circuit state machine to fix a race that caused transient double-opened circuits. Scope: code in serving runtime (sampler + control loop), controlplane controller, observability hooks, config schema, unit + integration tests, and k8s manifests. Risk: medium — affects routing decisions and failover sequencing; guarded behind feature flags and opt-in config. Rollout plan: 1) merge to main behind feature flag, 2) canary to internal tenants in us-west for 48h, 3) monitor new SLO and quality dashboards, 4) gradual increase of sampling fraction and shepherd aggressiveness. Related: ENG-2281 (graceful failovers post-incident), ENG-2314 (telemetry capture for fallback quality).

summary_of_changes: Implements a bounded probabilistic tenant fallback sampler and a regional traffic shepherd controller, wires telemetry for fallback attempts and outcomes, adds feature-flagged k8s manifests, and includes a hotfix for a circuit-state race. Tests and runbook included.
tests_and_benchmarks: Unit tests for sampler edge cases, integration tests exercising shepherd sequencing under synthetic load, e2e scenario to validate KV preservation, microbenchmarks showing median routing decision latency increase +0.6ms under sampling enabled. CI ran full test matrix; integration tests retried once due to flakiness and passed on rerun.
review_comments: Miguel Torres (2026-02-17): Great approach — can we add a guard so sampled fallback never routes to a model with different tokenization? Risk of client-facing corruption.
Evelyn Li (2026-02-18): The epoch token solves flapping but make sure controller persists last-seen epoch across restarts; otherwise we can re-open circuits prematurely.
Jordan Kim (2026-02-19): Integration test failed in first CI run with a race in shepherd start; please add deterministic startup ordering and a TTL to the epoch lock.
Miguel Torres (2026-02-22): Telemetry looks good, add a histogram for time-to-first-success after fallback so we can correlate quality regressions.
Evelyn Li (2026-02-24): Is the per-tenant cap enforced in the router policy or sampler? Make sure both enforcement and accounting are colocated to reduce drift under high concurrency.
author_responses: Asha Patel (2026-02-18): Added tokenization compatibility check in router_policy.go and unit tests to assert model variant compatibility before fallback.
Asha Patel (2026-02-19): Persisted epoch in controller state store and added startup reconciliation logic to shepherd. Also added TTL to epoch lock to prevent deadlocks.
Asha Patel (2026-02-20): Fixed startup race by sequencing shepherd init after config load in the controller; updated e2e to assert stable startup ordering.

Asha Patel (2026-02-23): Added time-to-first-success histogram and a new dashboard tile. Enforced per-tenant cap inside sampler and added an optimistic local counter in router policy for rapid checks.
Asha Patel (2026-02-25): Ran additional bench runs; sampling adds ~0.6ms median latency to routing decision, 95th still within SLO for canary tenants.
ci_checks: integration-tests: flaky (1st run failed) -> retried -> passed
operational_notes: Feature gated behind config.schema.v1.fallback.enabled and per-tenant flag. Shepherd has a conservatively low default sampling_fraction=0.02 and epoch_ttl=30s. Runbook updated with rollback steps: set fallback.enabled=false, manually clear epoch locks via admin tooling, and scale shepherd replicas to 0 if needed.
migration_and_config: Adds config/schema/v1/fallback.yaml with new keys: sampling_fraction, per_tenant_cap, epoch_ttl_seconds, shepherd_aggressiveness. No DB migrations required; controller persists epoch in existing controlplane key-value store under 'shepherd/epoch/<region>'.
observability_and_alerting: New metrics: telemetry.events.fallback_attempt_total, telemetry.events.fallback_success_total, telemetry.events.fallback_quality_score (gauge), telemetry.histograms.time_to_first_success_ms. Added dashboard fallback_quality.json and two alerts: ALERT_FALLBACK_QUALITY_DROP (fires when quality_score drops >10% for 5m) and ALERT_EPOCH_LOCK_LEAK (fires if epoch locks > expected by 60s).
